transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-04
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Emma (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Alicia (Head of ML, Northwood), Ben (Infra), Maya (PM)
Shared artifacts: 1) Redwood POC checklist deck (link: https://redwood.internal/poc-deck) 2) Benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/nwa)

--- Summary / Topics (auto-generated, may be rough) ---
- Goals: decide deployment pathway and success criteria for a 6-week POC.
- Topics: throughput/latency targets, dataset characteristics, latency vs cost tradeoffs, security/compliance items (SOC2, KMS, audit logs), timeline to pilot.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Emma: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh let's do quick intros, I'm Emma from Redwood, we do inference platform and I'll hand to Dan in a sec for the perf bits
[00:07] Alicia: hi all, Alicia from Northwood Analytics, we run a productized r-a-g flow for insurance claims summarization and a few internal classification tasks
[00:13] Ben: Ben here, infra lead, we'll need to figure networking and data residency constraints, we've got some on-prem tenants
[00:18] Maya: Maya product, timeline is tight, we want a pilot within 6 weeks if possible
[00:24] Daniel: great, Daniel Kim, I'm the solutions engineer, I'll cover workload sizing and benchmark plan, quick note, I'm gonna use the shorthand H for Hosted, D for Dedicated, P for Private

[01:02] Emma: high level, we want to map success criteria — usually teams pick 2 primary metrics: latency SLO (p95), and cost per 1k tokens or per inference call, then quality/regression thresholds tied to golden prompts
[01:18] Alicia: for us p95 latency under 400 ms for single-turn lookups is ideal, but we can tolerate up to 700ms during peaks, cost target is around $0.08 per thousand tokens if possible
[01:28] Daniel: ok that's helpful, can you confirm qps and average tokens per request?
[01:34] Alicia: yes average tokens 180, peak qps we expect 55 sustained for short bursts up to 120 for 2-3 minutes during batch windows

[02:10] Ben: question on deployment modes — our security team prefers Private (VPC/on-prem) for PHI-adjacent data, but business is tempted by Hosted for faster time-to-market, how do we structure a POC to evaluate both?
[02:21] Emma: good question, we usually recommend a two-track POC: start with Hosted to validate quality and baseline latency and cost, then run Dedicated or Private validation depending on security gating. Hosted gives fastest feedback because there's no infra setup. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and costs; Private gives you full network control and KMS integration but needs infra lead time

[03:05] Daniel: from sizing perspective, given avg tokens 180 and 55 qps sustained, that's ~9.9k tokens/sec at baseline, using our model estimates that'll map to approx 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs in Dedicated for low-latency config with 16k context. If you want headroom for bursts to 120 qps, bump to 3 GPUs or autoscale burst policy
[03:35] Ben: when you say A100-equivalent, do you mean Redwood's Dedicated sizing or raw GPU counts? we have mixed fleet in our colo so mapping matter
[03:42] Daniel: yes that's Redwood Dedicated sizing (we account for batching and KV cache too), raw GPU equivalence depends on quantization and model family, we'll include a spreadsheet mapping to your available hardware
n[04:17] Emma: note on caching — your usage pattern with lots of repeated context and retrieval keys can dramatically lower cost; our KV cache prefix helps but in Private you'll have more control over cache warming strategies

[05:00] Maya: what about benchmarks? we need to see both latency and quality drift across quantized models
[05:05] Daniel: we'll run the comparative benchmark: Hosted baseline with full FP model, Dedicated with INT8 / 4-bit quant profiles, and Private on your infra if possible. We'll measure p50/p95, throughput, token cost, and a quality delta on your golden prompts. Expect 72-hour runs to get realistic burst behavior

[06:00] Alicia: for the quality metric, we need a regression threshold — no more than 3% drop in rouge-like score on the summaries, or product team won't accept it
[06:09] Emma: noted, we'll tie the eval harness to that threshold and set automatic regression alerts. we'll also include an A/B fallback plan — if quantized model drops quality beyond threshold, auto-fallback to full-precision for those requests

[07:20] Ben: networking — Private requires V P C peering or direct connect, plus our audit logs must be shipped to our SIEM, is Redwood able to integrate with Splunk/Datadog?
[07:30] Daniel: yes we support log forwarding to Splunk, Datadog, and S3 buckets; for Private we can provide audit log endpoints and support KMS/HSM integration for key control. note that Private also increases lead time (we've seen 4-6 weeks for full on-prem integration)

[08:15] Alicia: SOC2 and ISO? we'll need the compliance pack to give our legal. Also data residency — some datasets cannot leave EU. Are there regional Hosted options?
[08:24] Emma: Redwood has regional hosted endpoints in NA and EU; SOC2 report and ISO docs will be shared. For EU-only data we can either run Dedicated in EU region or Private deploy in your EU colo. We'll share SOC2 pack and a short compliance checklist after call

[09:05] Maya: timeline — you said dedicated/d private take longer, does this jeopardize our 6-week pilot ask?
[09:12] Daniel: recommended path: Week 0-1: onboarding and hosted baseline; Week 2: run hosted benchmarks; Week 3: analyze results and optional Dedicated sizing; Week 4-5: Dedicated POC or Private setup depending on gating; Week 6: finalize pilot and handover. So we can meet 6-week pilot if we start with Hosted and concurrently run sizing work for Dedicated

[10:00] Emma: cost modeling — we will provide a cost worksheet that shows per-1k token and per-hour GPU burn for Dedicated tiers and an estimate for Hosted based on sample traces
[10:12] Ben: is there a minimum commit on Dedicated? also curious what automatic fallback looks like if Dedicated capacity hits limits
[10:17] Emma: Dedicated has reserved tiers (monthly commit) and burst options; fallback policy routes to compatible Hosted model or a lower-cost quantized variant depending on your policy. We'll include policy templates in the SOW

[11:05] Alicia: can Redwood's routing do content-based routing? e.g., PII requests go to Private while general requests go to Hosted?
[11:12] Daniel: yes, we support request-level routing by policy. You can tag requests and route them to different deployment modes. There is some complexity around latency when routing to Private if it's cross-region

[12:20] Maya: what metrics will you show in the console for the POC? product owner needs easy dashboard
[12:26] Emma: the Console shows per-route p50/p95, token cost, call volume, trace links and sample outputs. We'll add a custom dashboard for your golden prompts and fail-rate/regression flags

[13:00] Ben: about data handling — in Hosted we need to ensure data not retained beyond X days, can we set retention on request logs and inputs?
[13:08] Daniel: yes, Hosted has configurable retention windows; for stricter controls Private gives you full control. We'll capture the exact retention fields you need in SOW

[14:15] (Minor crosstalk, someone mutes/unmutes)
[15:00] Alicia: on benchmarks, we want to see tail latency under cold-start conditions and after warm cache, and also memory footprint for the model variants
[15:09] Daniel: we'll include cold-start scenarios in the 72-hour run and capture memory and GPU utilization samples. We'll also run simulated KV cache warming phases

[17:30] Emma: decision criteria framework suggestion: 1) if security gating is YES and cannot be relaxed -> Private; 2) if you need predictable high throughput with committed economics -> Dedicated; 3) if fastest validation and lowest startup time -> Hosted

[18:05] Ben: what about cost delta example? can you ballpark Hosted vs Dedicated for our workload?
[18:12] Daniel: ballpark — Hosted baseline op cost might be slightly higher per token at low volume but avoids commit. Dedicated, with a 12-month commit amortized, could reduce unit cost by ~20-35% depending on utilization. We'll put numbers in the pricing worksheet

[20:00] Emma: risks: Private lead time, Dedicated commit if utilization low, and quality regressions from quantization. Mitigations: staged rollout, canary tests, gating by quality evals

[22:00] Alicia: stakeholders alignment — security, legal, procurement need docs. procurement wants a 30-day cancellation in pilot, legal wants indemnity and data processing addendum

[23:10] Emma: we can do a pilot SOW with limited-term commitment and include a data processing addendum (DPA) and SOC2 attachments. procurement/redwood legal can iterate, we'll include that in the next steps

[24:00] Maya: are there integration tasks for our side beyond dataset share? e.g., instrumentation, SDKs, or webhooks?
[24:07] Daniel: minimal instrumentation — a small client wrapper or SDK call and S3 ingestion for the sample dataset. For Private there are extra steps for VPC peering and firewall rules which Ben will own

[26:00] Ben: we want to run the Private option on our EU colo for a subset of traffic. Is there a minimum infra footprint?
[26:08] Daniel: for a minimal Private footprint to meet your p95 target we'd recommend 2 GPUs with autoscale; exact count depends on model family and quantization. We'll draft a sizing table by the end of the week

[28:45] Alicia: what about monitoring alerts — who gets paged? we need SLOs and paging thresholds defined
[28:52] Emma: we'll propose an SLO baseline and suggested paging rules (e.g., p95 > 800ms or error rate > 2% triggers page). These are configurable in Console; we'll align on escalation path in the SOW

[31:10] Daniel: operational note: for the Dedicated baseline we recommend enabling continuous batching and a medium KV cache TTL to hit cost targets; we'll test sensitivity during the benchmark

[33:20] (brief silence, typing)
[34:00] Maya: success criteria recap — pilot success = meet p95 < 400ms OR acceptable fallback policy, cost within 20% of target, and no more than 3% quality regression on golden prompts. Also procurement approves pilot SOW

[34:18] Emma: yes that's a good recap, we will add pass/fail checks to each metric in the benchmark spreadsheet

[36:00] Alicia: one last question — if Dedicated saturates, is there an SLA on failover to Hosted?
[36:07] Daniel: SLA for Dedicated uptime is part of contract; failover behavior is defined by routing policy, we can do immediate fallback to Hosted with different latency profile. We'll show a template failover policy in SOW

[38:00] Ben: security deep dive — our security team will need details on KMS, HSM, key rotation cadence, and audit log schemas. Can Redwood share that?
[38:08] Emma: yes we'll share KMS/HSM integration doc and an audit log schema. We'll set a security workshop as a follow-up with Redwood security engineers

[40:00] (minor off-topic banter about weekend plans)

[42:00] Daniel: logistics for benchmarks — send sample traces and anonymized dataset to bench@redwood.ai, Daniel will provision tests, expect 48 hours for initial hosted run results, full 72-hr comparative results in about 7 days after start

[44:20] Maya: for timeline clarity — we need a kickoff next Monday to keep to 6-week cadence
[44:28] Emma: I'll propose a kickoff for 2025-11-10 at 9am PT, putting tentative invites now

[46:00] Alicia: ok thank you, this was super helpful. We'll prioritize dataset and traces and Ben will validate VPC options

[47:30] Emma: recap of next steps: send pricing + SOW draft, run hosted benchmark, schedule security deep dive, provide sample data and traces. Action owners agree?

[47:55] Ben: yes
[48:02] Daniel: yes
[48:05] Alicia: yes

[55:40] Emma: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and the benchmark sheet, talk soon
[55:50] (meeting ends)
